components.explanation: What both clips are made of, and the one decision this assignment turned on. The sheet is CUT from seven pose PNGs generated with GPT-6 for an earlier project - the generator recomposites every cut and exits unless it equals the source pixel for pixel, so 'the cut is lossless' is proved rather than claimed, and NO POSE FILE IS EVER EDITED. Three cells are cut legless, because the rig drives the legs under them; the other five keep their own painted legs and the leg clips switch the rig's off. The two leg textures and the blade are drawn by the same generator in the character's own two greys.

The looping clip, and the arithmetic under it. A 2D cutout rig: two Node2D legs keyed on rotation_degrees, as resource text, never built in code at runtime. Its length is DERIVED - two strides at 24 px against SPEED 96 gives 0.500 s exactly - so the cycle and the step dust share a clock and the planted foot and the puff under it are the same event. Front plus back is constant on every key, which is exact antiphase as arithmetic rather than as description. The seam rule that applies is the CONTINUOUS one: every interpolated track ends where it started.

The clip that commits: 18 frames at 30 fps, LOOP_NONE, with the body on a discrete frame track and the sword arm on a keyed cutout pivot. Both the arm's rotation AND its position are keyed, because a blade rotating about a fixed hilt inside the silhouette is a clock hand whichever way it turns. The hitbox's `monitoring` is a discrete track on the same timeline, which is the assignment's point about a gameplay fact not depending on a tween. Three read-back rules came out of the author playing it: the arc travels one way while the blade is visible, it finishes below the hand, and the hilt crosses the torso.

The assignment's hardest rule, and what it actually says. This project broke it on day one - a pose driver wrote the sprite's texture every _process and the new clip keyed the same node - and that driver is deleted. The interesting half came later: the rule is one authority per NODE, so a SECOND AnimationPlayer over a disjoint set of nodes breaks nothing, and the legs got their own. The read-back asserts the partition in both directions, because a partition checked one way round is only a subset. player.gd owns the state machine because committing is gameplay; player_anim.gd reads it, plays both players, and writes no animated property at all.

Which tick each clip advances on, which tick gameplay reads the active window on, and what the disagreement actually is. Both players are set to the PHYSICS callback mode rather than left at the engine's idle default, so writer and reader share a tick. The brief predicted what the default would cost and tagged the prediction [proposal]; the measurement was built to test it and found it wrong in sign - idle is one step EARLY, not late, and the cause is where the mixer's advance falls inside the frame rather than read latency. The claim underneath survived: the window opens at playhead 0.2000 in both modes. project.godot is here because the physics tick is 60 by being UNSET, and a tick that is the engine default is still the tick every frame count in this film is stated at.

What the clips play in, and what the footage rests on. The three-trap room, the backdrop and audio the contrast was judged against, the trap whose own warning window the swing's active window is sized against, and Assignment 6's step dust - which is here rather than excluded because the run cycle is timed to it: one puff per 24 px is the same event as one footfall, and the dust is how a viewer can see that the cycle and the game agree. The capture driver records all three takes and asserts its own outcome before a frame of it counts as evidence; the input-map check presses the real keys, because an action can exist with the wrong key on it and a test that only asks whether it exists stays green.

code_result_pairs.observation: C1 RESULT. take-c, PLAYED: held keys through the real input map, nothing teleported. The take asserts nine cycle wraps, both facings and twenty three dust puffs before a frame of it counts. It never crosses a trap, deliberately.

C2 RESULT. take-s, PLAYED: four fresh swings with a half-second gap, so none of them is a buffered second attack. The take asserts the window opened exactly four times and every clip ran its own 36 physics frames.
C3 RESULT. The partition read back out of the two committed resources, plus the mutation that puts one leg track back on the body player and the two assertions it turns red.
C4 RESULT. The recorded output of measure_clocks.gd, both modes, from evidence/a7/clocks.txt. It also states what the run CANNOT see, which is the jitter half of the prediction.

C5 RESULT. take-m, PLAYED: a direction held through two swings, then two swings jumped out of. The take asserts a hundred and eight frames of travelling swing with the gait playing under it, and two swings that left the floor without the swing counter moving.
C6 RESULT. The recorded section E output, and beside it mutation M7, whose point is that it still jumps. From evidence/a7/mutations.txt.
